content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, and built a full source ledger against the disclosure.

## What traced cleanly

Every claim limitation in claims 1–16 traces to an exact affirmative passage in `input/disclosure.md`: the branch-limit-below-sum-of-ratings premise, the per-channel contactor / connector current sensor / control-pilot interface / local connector identifier, the upstream branch current sensor, the isolated local bus, the four stored per-session values, the subtract-non-charging-load-and-safety-reserve allocation, sustaining-first then energy-deficit distribution, pilot send plus connector verification, verification interval after a reduced pilot command, one-at-a-time ordered shedding to a stored order, the three reclosure conditions with randomized delay, welded-contactor recording with inhibit-others plus local fault indicator, the signed token / last accepted branch limit / outage behaviour / token expiry, tamper-evident meter sequence, and the service-input mapping with agreement-before-storage. All 25 numerals resolve to exactly one part each and all appear in both the description and a figure brief. No drafting notes, placeholders, or unresolved alternatives remain, and the application text contains no "by way of example" shape language propping up a renderer's choice.

## What I am reporting

1. **Major — the connector-current sensing path is depicted inconsistently.** FIG. 2 draws a dashed sensing lead that exits the top of the channel and terminates in empty space, while FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 show the controller reaching the channels only through the isolated local bus, and the description's two connection inventories list only the bus and the branch current sensor. The coupling itself is supported (claim 1 recites it; the disclosure requires verification with the corresponding sensor), so the fix is to drop the dangling line rather than to invent a route the inventor never described.

2. **Minor — FIG. 4's "the flow ends" wording** asserts termination of the whole control process on a welded-contactor condition; the disclosure states only inhibition of the other contactors and operation of the fault indicator, and the description says only that step 216 is not reached. Reworded, the same geometry stands.

input.summary: Full preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the USER passage in input/conversation.md, with input/brief.md used only for formalities (no priority claim, no federal support, no means-plus-function, apparatus plus method classes). I traced every limitation of all sixteen claims, every one of the twenty-five numerals in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part and relationship in the field, summary, detailed description and abstract, and all four figure briefs (FIG. 1 through FIG. 4) to exact affirmative inventor passages. The core ledger is supported: branch limit lower than the sum of connector ratings; per-channel contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier; branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors as an independent safety input; isolated local bus to the connector interfaces and contactors; storage of charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current and energy-deficit value for each active connector; per-interval subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and a configurable safety reserve to obtain available charging current; minimum-sustaining assignment first, then remainder by energy deficit; pilot send and connector-sensor verification; reduced pilot command and verification interval; one-at-a-time ordered shedding in a stored order until measured branch current is below the branch limit; the three reclosure conditions including the randomized recovery delay; welded-contactor recording above a leakage threshold with inhibition of the other contactors on the branch and operation of a local fault indicator; network interface, signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit in nonvolatile memory, outage continuation, refusal of new sessions absent an unexpired token, tamper-evident meter sequence and upload on restoration; and the service-input mapping stored only after the responding sensing channel agrees with the commanded connector. Numeral integrity checked: each numeral means exactly one part, every numeral in the ledger appears in the description and on a figure, and no numeral appears in the description that is absent from the ledger. Text checks: claims and description use the same terms and relationships, the Brief Description of the Drawings matches the four briefs, the abstract is 146 words, no means-plus-function language appears, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. No cross-section views exist, so no section-line designation checks applied. Generic block outlines, the schematic square and circle sensor symbols, the rounded-rectangle vehicle and the flowchart shapes were treated as depiction conventions because the briefs and the Brief Description call the views schematic, the claims and description stay shape-neutral, and no proportion, count, material, taper, depth, runout or contact topology is verbalized. Two defects are reported, neither of which is an untraced invention limitation: a dangling dashed connector-current sensing lead in FIG. 2 that contradicts the connection inventories in FIG. 1, FIG. 3 and the description, and a statement in the FIG. 4 brief that the process flow ends on a welded-contactor condition, which the disclosure does not state and the description does not repeat. Both fixes are removals or rewordings that add no new technical assertion. No prior-art characterization in the Background was reported, since a later review traces those to prior_art/.

findings.title: FIG. 2 shows a dangling connector-current sensing lead that contradicts FIG. 1, FIG. 3 and the description's connection inventories
findings.where: figures/FIG-2.md (paragraph beginning "Apart from the dashes forming the outline of the dashed rectangle"); cross-checked against figures/FIG-1.md, figures/FIG-3.md, and draft/08-detailed-description.md paragraphs 4 and 9
findings.detail: FIG. 2 verbalizes a dedicated sensing connection that carries the measured connector current out of the connector channel by a route other than the isolated local bus, and leaves that line terminating in empty space, touching nothing. FIG. 1 shows no such path: the only things reaching connector-channel block 120 are the branch drop from the branch conductor and the isolated local bus branch, and the only dashed line in FIG. 1 is the branch-current-sensor lead. FIG. 3 likewise shows only two lines leaving the edge controller across its lower side, a solid line to the isolated local bus and a dashed line to the branch current sensor. The description matches FIG. 1 and FIG. 3 and not FIG. 2, stating that the controller "is coupled to the branch current sensor 104 and is coupled to the connector channels by an isolated local bus 108" and that "Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104", and it enumerates the bus contents as "the assigned current limits, the contactor commands and the pilot reports", omitting connector-current reports. The disclosure supports the coupling itself (the controller "verifies the resulting connector current with the corresponding current sensor", and claim 1 recites a controller coupled "to the connector current sensors"), but it never describes by what path the connector current reaches the controller: it says only that "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus." The FIG. 2 line therefore both asserts an untraced routing topology (a per-channel sensing lead separate from the isolated local bus, exiting the channel upward toward the branch conductor region) and leaves an unterminated connection that no other view or text accounts for.
findings.evidence: FIG-2.md: "Apart from the dashes forming the outline of the dashed rectangle, the drawing area contains exactly one dashed line, the sensing connection that carries the measured connector current out of the connector channel. It begins at the top of the circle outline and runs straight upward, right of and parallel to the solid vertical line and well clear of it, crossing the top side of the dashed rectangle and ending a short distance above that side, touching no other line and no leader." || FIG-1.md: "A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block and runs horizontally beneath the row of three blocks, representing an isolated local bus... A dashed line runs from the square outline down and left to the boundary of the edge controller block, representing the sensing connection." || FIG-3.md: "A solid line crosses the lower side of the large rectangle as the connection leaving the edge controller to the isolated local bus, and a dashed line crosses the lower side of the large rectangle as the connection leaving the edge controller to the branch current sensor." || draft/08: "Connections leave the edge controller 106 and lead to the isolated local bus 108 and to the branch current sensor 104, both of which are shown in FIG. 1." || disclosure.md (nearest passage, silent on the sensing path): "A controller communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-2.md, delete the entire paragraph beginning "Apart from the dashes forming the outline of the dashed rectangle..." and replace it with: "Every connection in the drawing area other than the outline of the dashed rectangle is solid." Leave the connector current sensor 124 shown as the circle outline in series on the horizontal run, and leave all other line work, numerals and leaders unchanged. No change is needed in FIG. 1, FIG. 3, the description or the claims: the controller's coupling to the connector current sensors remains recited in draft/08 ("The edge controller 106 is coupled to the connector current sensor 124 of that connector channel and receives the connector current measured by the connector current sensor 124") and in claim 1, without any figure asserting an undisclosed routing.

findings.title: FIG. 4 brief states that the process flow ends on a welded-contactor condition, which neither the disclosure nor the description states
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph beginning "The line from the welded-contactor isolation step to the conditional reclosure step"; cross-checked against draft/08-detailed-description.md, welded-contactor isolation step 214 and conditional reclosure step 216
findings.detail: The figure brief verbalizes that the whole control flow terminates when a welded-contactor condition has been recorded. The disclosure states only two consequences of that condition: "The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator." It does not state that the controller ceases the allocation loop. The description likewise never says the process ends; it says only that step 216 is "reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch" and that "While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed." The terminator symbol itself is an ordinary flowchart convention for a path that does not continue, but the words "the flow ends" convert it into an untraced operating-condition assertion that the controller stops running the allocation interval altogether, and the description contains no counterpart for it.
findings.evidence: FIG-4.md: "Where one has been recorded the flow ends at the welded-contactor isolation step, shown by a short horizontal line from the right edge of that rectangle ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator." || draft/08 (nearest text, no termination stated): "At a conditional reclosure step 216, reached where no welded-contactor condition has been recorded on the electrical branch..." and "While the welded-contactor condition stands, the inhibited contactors are not reclosed." || disclosure.md (nearest source passage, showing the gap): "The controller then inhibits the other contactors on the same branch and operates a local fault indicator."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, replace the sentence with: "Where one has been recorded the conditional reclosure step is not reached, shown by a short horizontal line from the right edge of that rectangle ending in an arrowhead at a small solid square terminator." The drawing geometry, the shape count, the numerals and the two return paths are unchanged; only the unsupported statement that the flow ends is removed.
